scalar.label: Scalar parameter
scalar.definition: Represents one value, such as n, start, or limit. Use it when the procedure needs an individual input rather than a collection. For example, n can indicate the problem size.

array.label: Array parameter
array.definition: Represents a collection of values accessed through indices. In A[n], A is the array and n identifies the position or dimension to use.

range.label: Range parameter
range.definition: Represents a segment bounded by a start and an end. The A[n]..[m] notation means working from position n through position m, usually to traverse or analyze part of an array.

object.label: Object parameter
object.definition: Represents a compound value created from a class, including its properties and methods. In Clase objeto, Clase is the type and objeto is the instance name received by the procedure.

action.label: Action
action.definition: An instruction that transforms data, stores a value, or prepares the algorithm's next step.

condition.label: Condition
condition.definition: An expression evaluated as true or false to choose which path to follow.

loop.label: Loop
loop.definition: A structure that repeats a block of instructions while a rule holds or across a range.

return.label: Return
return.definition: The instruction that ends one procedure path and sends a value back to its caller.

result.label: Result
result.definition: The data that the procedure produces and communicates when its work is complete.

path.label: Execution path
path.definition: The sequence of instructions that runs according to the algorithm's conditions and loops.

manualMode.defaultCode:
binarySearch(A[n], x, start, high) BEGIN
  IF (start > high) THEN BEGIN
    RETURN -1;
  END
  mid <- (start + high) / 2;
  IF (A[mid] = x) THEN BEGIN
    RETURN mid;
  END
  ELSE BEGIN
    IF (x < A[mid]) THEN BEGIN
      RETURN binarySearch(A, x, start, mid - 1);
    END
    ELSE BEGIN
      RETURN binarySearch(A, x, mid + 1, high);
    END
  END
END

divide_and_conquer.title: Divide and Conquer
divide_and_conquer.shortMessage: Split the problem into smaller parts and then combine the answers.
divide_and_conquer.plainMeaning: The algorithm breaks a large problem into smaller subproblems, solves them separately, and then combines the results.
howToRecognize: Several recursive calls appear.
Arguments shrink by division, midpoint, or split ranges.
The typical form is T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n).
divide_and_conquer.whyItMatters: It often leads to recursion-tree or Master-Theorem analysis. This is the family behind algorithms such as Merge Sort.
divide_and_conquer.commonMistake: Not every multiple-recursion pattern is Divide and Conquer. If it shrinks by subtraction and repeats subproblems, it may be Decrease and Get Conquered.

decrease_and_conquer.title: Decrease and Conquer
decrease_and_conquer.shortMessage: You reduce the problem step by step without opening too many branches.
decrease_and_conquer.plainMeaning: The algorithm solves the problem by reducing it to a slightly smaller version, such as n-1 or n-c.
howToRecognize: There is one dominant recursive call.
The argument decreases by subtraction.
The typical form is T(n) = T(n-b) + f(n).
decrease_and_conquer.whyItMatters: It usually creates deep but not explosive recursion trees. It is common in factorial or recursive sum examples.
decrease_and_conquer.commonMistake: If two or more recursive calls shrink by subtraction, this is no longer the simple case.

decrease_and_be_conquered.title: Decrease and Get Conquered
decrease_and_be_conquered.shortMessage: There are repeated branches, and that can explode if you do not store results.
decrease_and_be_conquered.plainMeaning: The algorithm opens several recursive calls that shrink by subtraction. Many branches can end up recomputing the same result again.
howToRecognize: There are two or more recursive calls.
Arguments go down like n-1, n-2, or n-c.
No table is detected to avoid repeated states.
The typical form is T(n) = aT(n-b) + f(n), with a > 1.
decrease_and_be_conquered.whyItMatters: It is the classic signal of recursive inefficiency and often suggests very fast growth.
decrease_and_be_conquered.commonMistake: Do not confuse it with Dynamic Programming. If memoization exists, the story changes.

dp_top_down.title: Top-down DP
dp_top_down.shortMessage: There is recursion with memory to avoid repeating work.
dp_top_down.plainMeaning: The algorithm starts from the large problem and goes down recursively, but before recalculating it checks whether that state was already stored.
howToRecognize: There is recursion.
Before computing, it checks an indexed table.
After computing, it stores the result.
dp_top_down.whyItMatters: It turns repetitive recursion into a much more efficient solution by solving each subproblem only once.
dp_top_down.commonMistake: Having an array is not enough. There must be real reuse of previous results.

dp_bottom_up.title: Bottom-up DP
dp_bottom_up.shortMessage: You build from small cases until you solve the whole problem.
dp_bottom_up.plainMeaning: The algorithm fills a table iteratively, starting from base cases and moving toward larger states.
howToRecognize: It does not need recursion.
Loops fill a table.
Each cell uses states that were already computed.
dp_bottom_up.whyItMatters: It avoids recursion-stack overhead and often has better constants when the table is filled in a regular way.
dp_bottom_up.commonMistake: Not every array filled inside a loop is DP. It must represent problem states.

greedy.title: Greedy
greedy.shortMessage: You make local decisions. It is useful, but it must be justified.
greedy.plainMeaning: The algorithm chooses the best available option at each step and keeps that decision.
howToRecognize: There is repeated local selection.
The decision is added to the solution.
There is no backtracking or reconsideration.
greedy.whyItMatters: It can be very fast, but it is only correct if greedy-choice property and optimal substructure are justified.
greedy.commonMistake: Something that looks locally reasonable is not automatically globally optimal.

backtracking.title: Backtracking
backtracking.shortMessage: You explore options and go back when a branch does not work.
backtracking.plainMeaning: The algorithm builds partial solutions, checks whether they remain valid, and goes back when it finds a contradiction.
howToRecognize: There is recursion.
A partial solution is modified.
After the recursive call, the modification is undone.
There are feasibility conditions.
backtracking.whyItMatters: It is better than brute force because it does not wait until the end to discard impossible solutions.
backtracking.commonMistake: If it also uses optimization bounds, it is probably already Branch and Bound.

branch_and_bound.title: Branch and Bound
branch_and_bound.shortMessage: You explore branches, but prune the ones that cannot beat the best solution.
branch_and_bound.plainMeaning: It is optimization-oriented backtracking. It uses bounds to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.
howToRecognize: There is a decision tree.
There is pruning.
There is comparison against a bound or the best known solution.
branch_and_bound.whyItMatters: It reduces unnecessary search while preserving optimality when the bounds are well designed.
branch_and_bound.commonMistake: Having an if-statement is not enough. There must be a bound that discards branches because they cannot improve the solution.

iterative.title: Iterative
iterative.shortMessage: It looks mainly like a loop-based algorithm.
iterative.plainMeaning: The algorithm repeats instructions through loops, without strong signs of recursion, memoization, or branch-based search.
howToRecognize: FOR, WHILE, or REPEAT appear.
There are no recursive calls.
The cost is usually analyzed by counting how many times each line runs.
iterative.whyItMatters: It helps explain per-line costs, summations, best and worst cases, and loop invariants.
iterative.commonMistake: An iterative algorithm can also be bottom-up DP or greedy. The detector only reports the most likely label.

unknown.title: Not conclusive yet
unknown.shortMessage: There are still not enough signals to classify the technique.
unknown.plainMeaning: The detector did not find a clear enough pattern in the AST.
howToRecognize: Code is missing.
Parsing has not produced an AST yet.
The structure does not match a covered technique.
unknown.whyItMatters: It is better not to classify than to sell the wrong technique.
unknown.commonMistake: Do not force a label just because the algorithm superficially resembles a known example.

explanations.branch_and_bound: This fragment explores branches recursively, backtracks over previous decisions, and also prunes using bound comparisons. That is why AALIE interprets it as Branch and Bound.
explanations.dp_top_down: This fragment checks a table before recalculating and then stores the computed result. That combination of recursion and memory is the typical sign of top-down Dynamic Programming.
explanations.dp_bottom_up: This fragment fills a table with loops, and each state depends on values that were already computed. That is why AALIE interprets it as bottom-up Dynamic Programming.
explanations.backtracking: This fragment builds a partial solution, explores recursively, and then undoes decisions to try other options. That pattern is characteristic of Backtracking.
explanations.divide_and_conquer: This fragment makes several recursive calls over subproblems split by halves, midpoint, or range partition. That is why AALIE interprets it as Divide and Conquer.
explanations.decrease_and_be_conquered: This fragment makes several recursive calls while reducing the size by subtraction. Since no table is consulted before computing, those subproblems may repeat. That is why AALIE interprets it as Decrease and Get Conquered.
explanations.decrease_and_conquer: This fragment reduces the problem by subtraction and keeps one dominant recursive call. That is why AALIE interprets it as Decrease and Conquer.
explanations.greedy: This fragment makes local decisions that remain in place without backtracking or reuse of previous states. That shape suggests a greedy strategy, although AALIE reports it cautiously.
explanations.iterative: Loops dominate here, and there are no clear signs of recursion, memoization, or branch-based search. That is why AALIE interprets it as an iterative algorithm.
explanations.unknown: There are not enough signals in the AST to classify the technique safely.

meta.title: About AALIE
meta.description: Learn more about AALIE, an educational platform for Algorithm Analysis and Design with visual support, step-by-step analysis, course content, and quizzes.

hero.title: Learn algorithms by seeing the process, not just the answer
hero.subtitle: We are an educational platform built to help you learn Algorithm Analysis and Design in a clearer, more visual, and more practical way.
hero.body: With AALIE, you can write pseudocode, analyze how it behaves, follow its execution step by step, and practice with course content and quizzes designed to reinforce what you learn in class.

why.title: Learning complexity should not feel like guessing a formula
why.paragraph1: In many algorithm exercises, the final answer is just a notation: O(n), Θ(n log n), O(n²). But if you cannot see the path, the answer does not teach much.
why.paragraph2: AALIE was created to show that path: how each line is counted, how summations are formed, how recurrences are interpreted, and when a result cannot be stated safely.

capabilities.title: What you can do with AALIE

write.title: Write or upload pseudocode
write.description: Use the editor to write your algorithms or import .txt files directly.

analyze.title: Review the analysis step by step
analyze.description: AALIE shows line costs, cost functions, and asymptotic notation when the analysis is supported.

recursive.title: Explore recursive algorithms
recursive.description: Study recurrences with methods such as the Master Theorem, recursion tree, iteration, and characteristic equation when they apply.

trace.title: Follow an execution
trace.description: Use traces to understand what happens during a concrete run of an algorithm.

quizzes.title: Practice with quizzes
quizzes.description: Reinforce concepts with topic-based questions and feedback.

export.title: Export reports
export.description: Generate Markdown, LaTeX, PDF, or ZIP reports for study, review, or submission.

ai.title: AI can help, but it does not replace the analysis
ai.paragraph1: AALIE may include an AI assistant to explain results, help with syntax, or compare ideas. But the formal analysis does not depend on an AI model guessing the complexity.
ai.paragraph2: The main analysis is produced by the system using defined rules, pseudocode structure, and supported methods. That makes the result easier to review, repeat, and discuss in class.
ai.microcopy: The assistant is optional. If it is not configured, the analyzer, course, examples, quizzes, and exports still work.

path.title: It does not just give you an answer
path.description: It shows how the answer is reached.

conservative.title: It does not pretend to know what it cannot support
conservative.description: If a case lacks enough evidence, AALIE should show it as partial, unsupported, or inconclusive.

classroom.title: It is built for class
classroom.description: It brings together an editor, analysis, examples, content, quizzes, and reports.

bilingual.title: It works in Spanish and English
bilingual.description: The interface and core content are available in both languages.

limits.title: What AALIE does not promise
limits.intro: AALIE is not designed to solve any program written in any language. It works with controlled pseudocode and with the types of analysis that the system currently supports.

items.realCode: It does not analyze real source code written in Python, Java, C++, or other languages.
items.teacher: It does not replace the teacher or classroom explanation.
items.space: It does not provide formal space complexity analysis.
items.average: It does not claim a universal average case without a model.
items.truth: It does not use AI as a source of mathematical truth.
items.advanced: Some techniques, such as backtracking, branch and bound, or greedy algorithms, may appear as learning content, but they do not always have full formal analysis support.

sections.title: Purpose and summary
paragraphs: We want you to clearly understand what information AALIE uses, why it may need it, and what control you have over it.

AALIE is an educational platform created to support learning and teaching Algorithm Analysis and Design. You can use many of its tools without creating an account. Other functions, such as saving profile-related information, using external artificial intelligence services, or voluntarily taking part in an academic study, may require additional information processing.

Our general rule is simple: we use only information that is reasonably necessary to provide AALIE's functions, protect the platform, and conduct academic activities that have been disclosed in advance.

sections.title: Data controller
paragraphs: The Data Controller for personal data managed directly by AALIE is Juan Camilo Cruz Parra.
Address and contact location: Manizales, Caldas, Colombia. Email: juan.cruz37552@ucaldas.edu.co. Phone: +57 321 465 0754.

sections.title: Academic context
paragraphs: AALIE was developed in an academic context related to the University of Caldas. This reference describes the project's educational context and does not, by itself, mean that the University of Caldas is responsible for every data processing activity carried out through the platform.

sections.title: Scope of this policy
paragraphs: This policy applies to people who use AALIE, whether or not they create an account. It also applies to people who choose optional features such as the artificial intelligence assistant and to people who voluntarily agree to participate in academic studies conducted through AALIE.

When you use a service provided by a third party, such as Google for sign-in or an external artificial intelligence provider, that third party may also apply its own terms and privacy policies to processing it performs directly.

sections.title: Processing principles
paragraphs: AALIE seeks to process personal data lawfully, transparently, and only for clear purposes. This means that we seek to collect only necessary information, avoid uses different from those disclosed, protect access to data, retain information for a reasonably necessary period, and allow people to understand and exercise their rights over it.
When the law requires authorization for processing, that authorization must be prior and informed and may be retained as evidence of the authorization.

sections.title: Information that may be processed
paragraphs: Depending on the features you use, AALIE may work with:
items: Pseudocode that you write or upload for analysis.
.txt files that you choose to open through the editor.
Questions or instructions that you send to the assistant.
Answers that you select in quizzes.
Information related to your progress through educational content.
Basic account information when you choose to sign in.
Results, costs, traces, recurrences, warnings, and reports derived from the analysis.
Any other information that you voluntarily enter into a feature that clearly requests it.
paragraphsAfter: You do not need to provide sensitive information to use AALIE normally.

sections.title: Account and Google sign-in
paragraphs: Creating an account is optional for features that AALIE makes available without authentication. If you choose to sign in with Google, AALIE may receive the basic information needed to recognize you and maintain your account, such as:

We may also retain information needed to maintain your session, protect your account, and apply the permissions that belong within the platform. AALIE does not need to know or store your Google password.
Signing in with Google does not automatically give AALIE access to Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar, or private content in other Google services.
items: Confirmation that your email has been verified.
Identifiers needed to link your sign-in to your AALIE account.

sections.title: Use without an account and technical identifiers
paragraphs: You can use certain AALIE features without personally identifying yourself. In these cases, the platform may use a random identifier to recognize in a limited way that different requests came from the same browser.

This helps protect the service, distribute resources reasonably, and enforce usage limits without needing your name or email address. AALIE does not seek to identify anonymous users through invasive device-tracking techniques. This identifier is not used for advertising or to follow your activity outside AALIE.

sections.title: Pseudocode and analysis
paragraphs: When you write pseudocode or upload a compatible file, AALIE needs to process that content to perform the function you requested. Depending on the case, this may provide complexity analysis, line costs, mathematical functions, asymptotic notation, recurrences, traces, explanations, warnings, or reports.

The editor exists for working with algorithms, not for storing personal documents. Avoid entering real names, identity documents, email addresses, confidential information, trade secrets, passwords, credentials, or any other data that is not necessary to analyze the algorithm in pseudocode.
Formal analysis is performed by the AALIE engine and does not depend on using an AI assistant or entering a personal key.

sections.title: .txt files
paragraphs: AALIE may allow you to open .txt files and bring their contents into the editor. This feature is intended to make it easier to write or import pseudocode. It is not intended to operate as personal file storage.
Before uploading a file, review its contents. If it contains private or confidential information that you do not need for the analysis, remove that information before using the file.

sections.title: Results and reports
paragraphs: Results generated by AALIE may include information derived from the pseudocode you provided. If you generate a report, it may contain the original algorithm, mathematical analysis, costs, recurrences, traces, warnings, and other information needed to represent the analysis performed.

The file you download comes under your control. You decide where to store it and with whom to share it. Always review a report before sharing it, because personal or confidential information you originally entered may also appear in the generated document.

sections.title: Educational activity and quizzes
paragraphs: AALIE may record information related to your educational activity, such as:
items: Strengths or topics that may be useful to study again.
paragraphsAfter: This information is used to help you continue your learning process and, where applicable, deterministically adapt future practice activities.
AALIE results are pedagogical. They are not, by themselves, an official grade, certification, academic record, or professional diagnosis of your abilities.

sections.title: Local storage in the browser
paragraphs: AALIE may save some information directly in your browser to remember preferences and provide a more continuous experience. For example, it may retain:

Data stored only in your browser may disappear if you clear site data, use private browsing, change browsers, or change devices. We do not recommend storing sensitive information on public, shared, or lab computers.
items: Temporary information needed to use a feature.

sections.title: Artificial intelligence assistant
paragraphs: AALIE's artificial intelligence features are optional. Formal algorithm analysis does not depend on using an AI assistant.
When you choose to use it, the provider generating the response may need to receive information related to your request, such as:

This information is sent only when you use a feature that requires the external provider. Signing in to AALIE does not mean that your profile data is automatically sent to an artificial intelligence provider.

External providers may apply their own policies regarding data processing, retention, and location. Do not use the assistant with sensitive information, secrets, credentials, private information about other people, or confidential material that you are not authorized to share.
items: The pseudocode you are asking about.
Visible information relevant to understanding your question.
A recent part of the conversation needed to maintain context.

sections.title: Personal keys for AI providers
paragraphs: AALIE may allow you to use a personal key from an artificial intelligence provider. If you choose to do so, the key is used only to attempt the requests that you initiate through the relevant features.
Using a personal key may create costs, consume quotas, or be subject to conditions set directly by the provider. AALIE is not a service intended to manage enterprise secrets or credentials.

Do not share your key with other people and avoid using or storing it on public or shared computers. If you suspect that a key was exposed, revoke it directly through the relevant provider's platform.

sections.title: Information AALIE does not need
paragraphs: AALIE does not need the following for its ordinary operation:
items: Information about sex life or sexual orientation.
Information about racial or ethnic origin.
paragraphsAfter: Colombian law provides special protection for sensitive data and restricts its processing. The fact that a text box technically allows certain information to be entered does not mean that AALIE needs or requests it. Do not enter unnecessary sensitive information.

sections.title: Processing purposes
paragraphs: Information processed through AALIE may be used to:
items: Analyze algorithms and generate their results.
Create and maintain accounts when the user requests it.
Generate reports and answer requests made to the AI assistant.
Prevent abuse, protect availability, administer permissions, detect errors, and investigate security incidents.
Conduct academic studies only when there is valid participation for that purpose.
paragraphsAfter: We will not use the information for a substantially different purpose without first meeting the applicable information and authorization requirements.

sections.title: Research and ordinary use
paragraphs: AALIE may be used as a tool in research related to education, algorithms, learning, or evaluation of the platform itself. However, there is a clear separation between using AALIE and participating in research.
Creating an account, signing in, using the analyzer, taking a quiz, or opening educational content does not mean that you accepted participation in a study.

sections.title: Voluntary participation in studies and test environments
paragraphs: When a study requires your participation, AALIE must present it separately and explain the necessary information before recording your participation. Participation is voluntary, and where applicable you may withdraw consent according to the conditions provided for the study.

In test environments or experiments, use of the software may be limited to selected or invited users. You may choose not to take part in the experiment. If you do not wish to participate, you may contact us to request deletion of the associated data where legally permitted. This choice may mean that you lose access to the application or to experimental-environment features because access may depend on selected participation.
Refusing to participate or withdrawing from a study should not, solely for that reason, become a sanction within AALIE's ordinary educational use.

sections.title: Data a study may use
paragraphs: Depending on the study, data may include:
items: Measurements defined in advance by the protocol.
Activities performed within the features being studied.
Information needed to identify which version of the educational activity was used.
paragraphsAfter: Each study may limit the information it collects even further. The fact that AALIE can access other information as part of its normal operation does not mean that the information automatically becomes part of a research study.

sections.title: Data excluded from the academic dataset
paragraphs: As a general rule, datasets intended for academic analysis should not directly include:
items: Data used only to maintain your session.
Complete questions sent to an AI assistant.
Complete answers generated by that assistant.
paragraphsAfter: If future research needed to use different information, it would have to be specifically disclosed and the applicable authorizations or approvals obtained.

sections.title: Pseudonymization and identity protection
paragraphs: When you agree to participate in a study, AALIE may associate your participation with a code created specifically for that study. The goal is for information used in academic analysis to work primarily with a pseudonymous identity rather than your name or email address.

Separating your name from data used in a study considerably reduces direct exposure of your identity. However, while additional information exists that can legitimately link those records back to you, the data continues to receive the protection applicable to personal data. AALIE does not present pseudonymization as absolute anonymity.

sections.title: Withdrawal from research
paragraphs: Withdrawing from research does not automatically delete your AALIE account. Likewise, stopping your use of AALIE does not automatically change the status of an academic participation that was previously recorded.

If you participate in a study, the study-specific conditions will explain what happens to information already collected when you withdraw consent. The platform will seek to stop collecting new experimental information from a person who has withdrawn, unless a legal obligation requires otherwise.

sections.title: External services
paragraphs: AALIE needs certain external services to provide some of its functions. These may include hosting and infrastructure, authentication, artificial intelligence, security, communications, and other services needed to operate the platform.

Google is involved when you choose Google sign-in. Artificial intelligence providers are involved only when you use features that require their models. External providers receive only the information needed for the relevant function under the terms applicable to that integration. AALIE does not sell databases to these providers.

sections.title: International transfers
paragraphs: Some providers used to operate AALIE may be located in or process information outside Colombia. This may occur, for example, with infrastructure, authentication, or artificial intelligence services.

When processing involves the transmission or transfer of personal data internationally, the rules and safeguards required by Colombian law for the relevant case will apply. Using a foreign provider does not, by itself, authorize unlimited use of the information.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: AALIE adopts reasonable measures to protect information against loss, alteration, unauthorized access, or misuse. Among other measures, we seek to limit who can access information, separate functions that do not need to share data, protect communications, reduce the amount of information stored, and establish controls against abusive use.
No service connected to the Internet can guarantee absolute security. You can also help protect your information.
items: Do not enter secrets in the editor or assistant.
Tell us about any possible security incident.

sections.title: Children and adolescents
paragraphs: AALIE has an educational purpose and may be used in contexts involving children or adolescents. Their personal data receives enhanced protection.

When an activity requires processing a minor's personal data, their prevailing rights, best interests, and applicable authorizations must be respected. Research involving minors must also establish the specific participation, consent, or authorization conditions that apply. AALIE does not consider ordinary platform use a substitute for these safeguards.

sections.title: Data subject rights
paragraphs: As the data subject, you have the rights recognized by Colombian law, including:
items: Know which personal data is being processed.
Know how your data has been used.
Request proof of authorization when applicable.
Access your data free of charge.
Request revocation of authorization when applicable.
Go to the Superintendence of Industry and Commerce when the legal requirements are met.
paragraphsAfter: These rights are recognized in Law 1581 of 2012. Deletion or revocation may be limited when a legal obligation or legitimate reason requires certain information to be retained.

sections.title: Requests and identity verification
paragraphs: You may submit questions, requests, or complaints about your personal data to the Data Controller. Your request must allow us to know who you are, which right you want to exercise, and what information it concerns.

We may request information reasonably necessary to verify that the request comes from the data subject or a person legally authorized to act on their behalf. Questions and complaints will be handled within the time limits established by applicable Colombian law.

sections.title: Account and data deletion
paragraphs: You may request deletion of information associated with your account where legally permitted. Deleting an account does not necessarily mean that all records disappear immediately.

It may be necessary to temporarily retain information to comply with legal obligations, handle requests or complaints, protect security, investigate fraud or abuse, honor commitments validly made in research, or complete normal backup and deletion cycles. When there is no longer a valid reason to retain the information, it must be deleted or no longer kept personally associated with you, as applicable.

sections.title: Information retention
paragraphs: We retain data only while there is a valid purpose for doing so. AALIE's general database will remain in effect while the platform operates and for any additional period needed to comply with legal obligations, handle requests, protect security, or properly close its operations.

Information associated with an account may be retained while the account remains active or until a valid deletion request is processed, subject to legal exceptions. Information stored only in your browser will remain according to that browser's settings and may be deleted by you.

Each research study may establish its own retention period. When it does, that period must be disclosed as part of the study conditions. We will not retain information indefinitely merely because it might be useful in the future.

sections.title: Advertising, profiles, and third-party data
paragraphs: AALIE does not sell personal information. AALIE does not use your data to provide personalized advertising. AALIE does not build commercial profiles about students, teachers, or other users.
Information about your quiz performance is used for educational purposes and not to determine which products to offer you or which advertisements to show you.

Do not enter another person's personal information into AALIE unless you have the right and authorization to do so. We do not need a person's real name to analyze an algorithm. When you can use fictional or generic data, that is normally the more appropriate choice.

sections.title: Legal requests
paragraphs: We may provide information when there is a legal obligation, a valid order from a competent authority, or another circumstance permitted by applicable law. In those cases, we will seek to limit the information provided to what is necessary to respond to the relevant request.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: This policy may be updated when AALIE's functions, processing practices, providers, academic activities, or applicable law change.

Substantial changes will be communicated reasonably before new conditions begin to apply when necessary. A new purpose that requires additional authorization will not become automatically authorized simply because this policy was updated. The version and update date will remain visible so that the policy in effect can be identified.

sections.title: Effective date, authority, and final contact
paragraphs: This Privacy and Personal Data Processing Policy takes effect on August 21, 2026. It will remain in effect while AALIE continues the processing described here and will be replaced when a new version is formally published. The validity of each set of information depends on the purpose for which it was obtained and the retention periods explained in this policy or, where applicable, in the specific conditions of a study.

In Colombia, the authority responsible for personal data protection is the Superintendence of Industry and Commerce. You may contact it in the cases and after the prior procedures established by Colombian law.

For questions about this policy, personal data processing, privacy, information deletion, or exercising your rights, contact Juan Camilo Cruz Parra, AALIE's Data Controller, in Manizales, Caldas, Colombia, at juan.cruz37552@ucaldas.edu.co or +57 321 465 0754.

assistant.title: AI assistant
assistant.paragraph1: The AI assistant is optional. It can help you understand a result, fix syntax, compare explanations, or ask questions about algorithm analysis.
assistant.paragraph2: To respond, the assistant may receive information such as: your question, the visible pseudocode, the analysis result, warnings generated by AALIE, visible traces or recurrences, the panel or section you are using, and recent conversation history within the assistant.
assistant.paragraph3: If the assistant is connected to an external provider, that information may be sent to that provider to generate the response. The provider may process it according to its own policies, terms, and technical configuration.
assistant.paragraph4: Do not use the AI assistant with sensitive, private, confidential, secret information, or information belonging to third parties.

apiKeys.title: Personal API keys
apiKeys.paragraph1: Some AALIE deployments may allow you to enter your own API key to enable AI features. This is known as Bring Your Own Key.
apiKeys.paragraph2: If you choose to use a personal API key: it may generate costs on your provider account, it may be subject to the provider's limits, quotas, and policies, it may be sent to the AALIE backend to make the request to the configured provider, it should not be used on shared computers, it should be removed when you finish, it should not be shared with others, and it should not be included inside pseudocode or inside questions to the assistant.
apiKeys.paragraph3: Your API key is not used to calculate algorithm complexity. It only enables features associated with the AI assistant.
apiKeys.warning: AALIE is not meant to be an enterprise secret manager. If a deployment saves the API key in the browser, that decision carries risks: extensions, malicious scripts, local machine access, or shared device use could expose it.

localStorage.title: Local storage in the browser
localStorage.paragraph1: AALIE may use browser local storage to save preferences and progress. This storage resides on the device you are using.
localStorage.paragraph2: It may include, for example: selected language, module progress, quiz attempts, usage preferences, temporary interface states, and the personal API key only if the interface offers that option and you choose to save it.
localStorage.paragraph3: Do not use shared devices to store sensitive information. If you use AALIE on a public, lab, or someone else's computer, clear the site data when you finish.

security.title: Security
security.paragraph1: AALIE applies a minimization policy: use only the information necessary to provide its educational functions.
security.paragraph2: However, no web system eliminates all risks. The main risks you should be aware of are:

items.editor: If you paste sensitive information in the editor, it could be included in results or reports.
items.assistant: If you use the AI assistant, the context may be sent to an external provider.
items.key: If you save an API key on a shared browser, someone else could access it.
items.report: If you share a report, you will be sharing the content included in that file.
items.browser: If you clear browser data, you could lose your local progress.

exports.title: Reports and exports
exports.paragraph1: When you generate reports, AALIE may include information such as: original pseudocode, analysis results, line costs, traces, recurrences, warnings, technical metadata, snapshot identifiers, content hash, and institutional report information.
exports.paragraph2: The purpose of this data is to keep the report consistent with what you saw on screen.
exports.paragraph3: Before sharing a report, check that it does not include private pseudocode, sensitive data, keys, names, internal comments, or any information you do not want to disclose.

providers.title: External providers
providers.paragraph1: Google is used only as an optional identity provider. Sign-in uses the provider's basic identity permissions; AALIE does not request access to Gmail, Drive, Calendar, or other Google products.
providers.paragraph2: To maintain the account and session, AALIE stores basic user data and technical authentication records in PostgreSQL. When Better Auth persists OAuth credentials returned by Google, AALIE configures them to be encrypted before storage.
providers.paragraph3: Data obtained through Google is not sold, is not used for advertising, and is not sent to an AI provider merely because you signed in. Signing in also does not constitute consent to participate in research.

rights.title: Rights and requests
rights.paragraph1: You can contact the team if you have questions about this policy or about the use of information in AALIE.
rights.paragraph2: Depending on the case, you may request information about data related to you, ask for correction, update, deletion, or clarification about the processing of personal information that may be under the team's responsibility.
rights.paragraph3: Core features can be used without an account and, at this stage, quiz progress continues to be stored locally in the browser. You can delete that data from the browser. For data associated with a Google-created account, you can contact the team to make applicable access, correction, or deletion requests.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.paragraph1: We may update this policy when AALIE changes, especially if analytics, progress synchronization, new AI providers, new export formats, institutional integrations, or changes to API-key and authentication-data handling are introduced.
changes.paragraph2: When the policy changes, the last modified date will be updated.

By accessing or using AALIE, you accept these terms to the extent permitted by applicable law.

items.title: AALIE is an educational tool
items.description: Its results support learning and exploration, but they do not replace the mathematical, academic, or professional review that may be required.

items.title: Analysis coverage has limits
items.description: The system may abstain, show warnings, or produce partial results when a case exceeds its grammar, methods, or available evidence.

items.title: AI is optional support
items.description: Responses generated by language models may be inaccurate and must be checked. The assistant does not replace AALIE's deterministic engine.

sections.title: 1. Nature and purpose of AALIE
paragraphs: AALIE, short for Algorithm Analysis Learning Interactive Environment, is primarily an educational and academic software platform. Its purpose is to support learning, teaching, exploration, and analysis of algorithms and computational complexity.

Depending on the available version, the Service may include pseudocode editing and processing, iterative and recursive analysis, supported recurrence solving, traces, recursion trees, cost calculations, examples, courses, quizzes, exports, AI-assisted features, and compatible file uploads.

sections.title: 2. Educational nature of results
paragraphs: Results produced by AALIE are educational and supportive in nature. Although the engine uses rules designed to produce reproducible results within its coverage, no result should be treated as infallible.

Analysis may be incorrect, incomplete, partial, or inapplicable when pseudocode, variable relationships, recurrences, termination conditions, probability models, or symbolic complexity exceed what the system can safely interpret. Review every result before using it in academic work, evaluations, publications, research, professional work, or any other decision.

sections.title: 3. Heuristics and inconclusive analysis
paragraphs: Some features use conservative heuristics. When AALIE lacks enough evidence for a reliable conclusion, it may produce a partial result, identify an unsupported construction, show a warning, or decline to infer a specific complexity.
The absence of a conclusion does not mean that an algorithm has no mathematically determinable complexity. It may mean that the case exceeds AALIE's coverage, assumptions, or technical limits.

sections.title: 4. Execution traces
paragraphs: Traces, trees, walks, diagrams, and other execution representations are educational aids.

An execution with concrete values is not a general mathematical proof and does not guarantee behavior for every input size. It may be limited by depth, steps, resources, or other safety measures. Time and relative-cost estimates are not necessarily hardware benchmarks.

sections.title: 5. Exports and generated documents
paragraphs: AALIE may generate reports and documents derived from an analysis. They may include pseudocode, results, methods, recurrences, traces, tables, warnings, diagrams, and technical identifiers.

An export represents the analysis state at the time it was generated. It is not a certification, academic validation, peer review, or institutional approval. Warnings are an integral part of the report and must not be removed to make the result appear stronger than it is.

sections.title: 6. PDF, LaTeX, and technical dependencies
paragraphs: Some formats depend on additional technical components. PDF generation may require LaTeX tools available in the infrastructure where AALIE runs.

An export may fail temporarily, one format may be available while another is not, appearance may vary, or some elements may require an additional transformation. AALIE does not guarantee permanent availability of every format.

sections.title: 7. Language-model assistance
paragraphs: AALIE may offer optional features based on language models or external AI providers. These features are auxiliary and are not the source of truth for deterministic analysis.

Responses may contain errors, omissions, incomplete explanations, inaccurate claims, invalid code, or pseudocode that is incompatible with AALIE's grammar. Check them before use. Availability may depend on the provider, connection, model, quotas, limits, latency, policies, API changes, and valid credentials.

sections.title: 8. Third-party services
paragraphs: AALIE may interact with third parties for authentication, language models, infrastructure, hosting, software distribution, or other specific features.

Those services may also be subject to their own terms, policies, and limitations. AALIE does not control their availability, continuity, technical changes, or internal operation. A third-party interruption or change may affect a feature temporarily or permanently.

sections.title: 9. Sign-in with Google
paragraphs: AALIE allows users to sign in with Google to establish an identity within the Platform and enable account-related features.

AALIE will request only the data and permissions needed for that purpose, as described in the Privacy Policy and authorization interface. Google is not responsible for AALIE, its educational results, or the Platform's operation. Users must also comply with the terms applicable to their Google Account.

sections.title: 10. Access without an account
paragraphs: Where the Platform allows it, some features may be used without creating an account or signing in. Anonymous access may have different limits from authenticated access.

AALIE may apply controls to prevent abuse, reduce malicious automation, protect availability, control resources, and maintain fair use. Access without authentication does not create a permanent right to use a feature without limits.

sections.title: 11. Usage limits
paragraphs: AALIE may set limits for particular operations. Limits may depend on the user, authentication, operation, computational cost, available resources, external services, or observed behavior.
Operations with different costs may have different limits. AALIE may adjust them when necessary to maintain Service stability, security, or sustainability.

sections.title: 12. User accounts
paragraphs: When you use an AALIE account, you must use only authentication mechanisms you are legitimately authorized to access.

You may not use another person's account, impersonate someone, manipulate sessions, alter tokens, obtain higher privileges, bypass authorization controls, or access other users' data. AALIE may invalidate sessions or restrict access for technical or security reasons.

sections.title: 13. Roles and privileges
paragraphs: AALIE may distinguish between regular and administrative users. Creating an account does not automatically grant administrative privileges.

Only expressly authorized people may perform administrative functions. You may not alter your role, grant yourself privileges, manipulate permission requests, or access administrative endpoints without authorization.

sections.title: 14. Permitted use
paragraphs: You may use AALIE for lawful purposes consistent with its educational nature, including individual learning, teaching, classroom demonstrations, academic activities, experimentation, exercises, research, and critical evaluation of analysis methods.
You may also create material derived from your own analyses provided that you respect these terms, third-party rights, and applicable academic rules.

sections.title: 15. Prohibited use
paragraphs: You may not use AALIE to:
items: Compromise the security of the Platform or other systems.
Obtain unauthorized access to accounts, data, endpoints, or internal components.
Conduct attacks, abusive scraping, or automated loads that degrade the Service.
Evade limits, manipulate sessions, or extract secrets and credentials.
Distribute malware, exploit vulnerabilities to harm others, or interfere with infrastructure.
Use the Platform for unlawful purposes.
Deliberately present a result as a mathematical proof, certification, or institutional conclusion beyond the scope in which AALIE produced it.

sections.title: 16. User-provided content
paragraphs: You retain the rights you legally hold in pseudocode, algorithms, text, files, and other content you enter into AALIE.

When using a function that processes that content, you represent that you have the necessary rights or permissions. Do not upload material whose processing would infringe copyright, trade secrets, confidentiality agreements, third-party rights, or applicable law.
Avoid entering passwords, API keys, tokens, secrets, confidential information, or unnecessary personal data.

sections.title: 17. Technical processing of content
paragraphs: To provide the Service, AALIE may technically process the content you provide. Processing may include parsing, transformation, analysis, controlled execution, trace generation, snapshot construction, and report generation.
When an AI feature requires information to be sent to an external provider, that processing will be described in the Privacy Policy and the relevant interface.

sections.title: 18. AALIE intellectual property
paragraphs: Unless an applicable license states otherwise, AALIE's software, interface, visual identity, documentation, original materials, content organization, and other proprietary elements are protected by applicable intellectual-property rules.
Public access does not transfer rights. Components released under open-source licenses are governed by those licenses, and third-party licenses remain applicable to their components.

sections.title: 19. Institutional material and marks
paragraphs: AALIE may include names, logos, academic references, or other elements associated with participating institutions or the project's academic context.

Their inclusion does not grant rights to reuse institutional marks outside uses authorized by their owners. A report containing institutional elements does not mean that its content was reviewed or approved by the relevant institution.

sections.title: 20. Quizzes and educational content
paragraphs: Quizzes, exercises, examples, and other educational content are intended for practice and learning.

Unless expressly stated otherwise, they are not certifications, official academic grades, or substitutes for institutional assessments. They may be updated, corrected, withdrawn, or contain errors that are corrected over time. Adaptive selection does not constitute a professional educational diagnosis.

sections.title: 21. Academic integrity
paragraphs: AALIE is a learning aid, not a mechanism for avoiding academic responsibilities.

Each institution, teacher, or activity may set specific rules for digital tools or automated assistance. You are responsible for knowing and following the rules applicable to your course, assessment, or research. The fact that AALIE can perform an analysis does not mean its use is allowed in every context.

sections.title: 22. Research and academic studies
paragraphs: AALIE may be used in academic research or educational evaluation. Participation in a study must be distinguished from ordinary use of the Platform.

Visiting AALIE, creating an account, signing in with Google, or using the analyzer does not by itself constitute consent to participate in research. Any study requiring participation, additional data, or specific consent must explain that through the appropriate information and mechanisms.

sections.title: 23. Experimental data and pseudonymization
paragraphs: When AALIE is used in an authorized study, experimental data will be handled according to the information provided to participants, the Privacy Policy, and applicable rules.
Pseudonymization or aggregation reduces direct identification, but does not automatically make information anonymous or remove applicable legal obligations.

sections.title: 24. Availability and continuity
paragraphs: AALIE is provided according to the availability of its infrastructure, providers, and technical resources. It may experience interruptions because of maintenance, errors, configuration changes, security incidents, or third-party failures.
The Service is not guaranteed to be continuous, timely, compatible with every device, or error-free.

sections.title: 25. Changes to features
paragraphs: The project may add, modify, correct, limit, or remove features, algorithms, content, technical providers, and export formats.
When a change substantially affects rights or access conditions, AALIE will seek to communicate it appropriately.

sections.title: 26. No guarantee of permanent retention
paragraphs: Unless a feature expressly states otherwise, you should not use AALIE as the sole storage system for important information.

Keep independent copies of your algorithms, reports, work, files, results, and academic information. Clearing browser data, changing devices, or using another browser may affect information stored locally.

sections.title: 27. Security
paragraphs: AALIE applies reasonable technical measures intended to protect its infrastructure and processed data. However, no system connected to the Internet can guarantee absolute security.
If you identify a vulnerability, report it responsibly and do not exploit it to access information, alter data, interrupt services, or obtain privileges.

sections.title: 28. Privacy and personal data
paragraphs: Personal-data processing associated with AALIE is governed primarily by the Privacy Policy, which forms part of the documentation applicable to the Service.
If the two documents differ regarding a specific personal-data process, the provision that specifically describes that process will apply, without prejudice to rights recognized by applicable law.

sections.title: 29. Account deletion and closure
paragraphs: When AALIE enables account-deletion mechanisms, you may request deletion of associated information according to the Privacy Policy and applicable legal or technical obligations.
Some records may be retained for reasonable periods when needed for security, fraud or abuse prevention, legal compliance, dispute resolution, or backups subject to normal deletion cycles.

sections.title: 30. Suspension or restriction
paragraphs: AALIE may temporarily or permanently restrict access for reasons related to security, abuse, breach of these terms, infrastructure impact, fraud, unauthorized access, legal noncompliance, or harmful automation.
Where reasonably possible, contact channels will be available to review the situation.

sections.title: 31. Disclaimer of warranties
paragraphs: To the extent permitted by applicable law, AALIE is provided as is and as available.

AALIE does not absolutely guarantee mathematical accuracy, fitness for a particular purpose, permanent availability, compatibility with all pseudocode, academic validity, institutional acceptance of a report, or the accuracy of third-party or language-model responses. Warnings shown by the system are part of the conditions under which each result is provided.

sections.title: 32. Limitation of liability
paragraphs: To the extent permitted by applicable law, the team responsible for AALIE will not be liable for harm arising exclusively from use that violates these terms or from relying, without reasonable verification, on results expressly presented as educational support.

This may include harm arising from an incorrect analysis, an AI response, loss of local progress, an interruption, export errors, technical incompatibilities, or academic decisions made without independent review. Nothing in these terms excludes liability that cannot legally be excluded.

sections.title: 33. User responsibility
paragraphs: You are responsible for verifying information you use, keeping copies of important files, protecting your account, following academic rules, using the Platform lawfully, avoiding data you should not share, reviewing warnings, and checking results before presenting or using them in a formal context.

sections.title: 34. External links and resources
paragraphs: AALIE may include links to documentation, articles, providers, libraries, educational resources, and other external sites.
Those resources are managed by their respective operators. Including a link does not mean that AALIE approves their content or accepts responsibility for their practices, availability, or terms.

sections.title: 35. Changes to these Terms
paragraphs: These terms may be updated to reflect new features, technical changes, authentication systems, operational practices, legal requirements, third-party services, or research activities.

The update date appears at the beginning. When a change is material and reasonably requires notice, AALIE may communicate it through the Platform. Continued use after it takes effect may be subject to the updated version.

sections.title: 36. Termination of the Service
paragraphs: The project may suspend, transform, or terminate all or part of the Service.

Where reasonably possible, it will seek to provide advance information about significant changes. Termination does not require indefinite maintenance of infrastructure, external providers, or available storage.

sections.title: 37. Governing law
paragraphs: These terms will be interpreted under the applicable laws of the Republic of Colombia, without prejudice to mandatory rules that apply to the user's circumstances.
Before beginning a formal dispute, the parties will reasonably seek to resolve the issue through the available contact channels.

sections.title: 38. Severability
paragraphs: If a provision is declared invalid, unenforceable, or contrary to a mandatory rule, that decision will not automatically affect the validity of the remaining provisions.
The affected provision will be interpreted, within legal limits, as closely as possible to its original purpose.

sections.title: 39. No waiver

sections.title: 40. Entire applicable framework
paragraphs: These terms, together with the Privacy Policy and feature-specific notices, form the general framework applicable to use of AALIE.
When a feature displays additional terms or notices, they supplement this document for that feature.

sections.title: 41. Contact

examples.title: Algorithm Catalog

bogo-sort.title: Bogo Sort
bogo-sort.summary: An intentionally extreme teaching sample used to contrast an inefficient iterative sorter with the rest of the catalog.

bubble-sort.title: Bubble Sort
bubble-sort.summary: Sorts by comparing adjacent elements and works as a stable reference for quadratic iterative cases.

bucket-sort.title: Bucket Sort
bucket-sort.summary: Iterative bucket-distribution skeleton kept hidden until a grammar-friendly version is fully validated.

counting-sort.title: Counting Sort
counting-sort.summary: Counts frequencies and rebuilds the array in several linear passes over indices and occurrences.

dutch-national-flag.title: Dutch National Flag
dutch-national-flag.summary: Maintains three regions and is useful to study linear partitions with multiple pointers.

euclides-iterativo-mcd.title: Iterative Euclid (GCD)
euclides-iterativo-mcd.summary: A short and reliable sample to study a loop with geometric reduction on the state size.

factorial-iterativo.title: Iterative factorial
factorial-iterativo.summary: A basic linear sample that advances a simple control variable while accumulating a product.

flood-fill-iterativo.title: Iterative Flood Fill
flood-fill-iterativo.summary: A grid sample with an explicit stack; kept hidden until a robust variant for large traces is validated.

heapsort.title: Heapsort
heapsort.summary: Compact version built around iterative heapify; disabled until heap support is validated more thoroughly.

insertion-sort.title: Insertion Sort
insertion-sort.summary: Builds the sorted array by inserting each key into place and exposes a classic inner while loop.

jump-search.title: Jump Search
jump-search.summary: Alternates block jumps with a short linear scan and is useful to study two consecutive loops.

kadane.title: Kadane
kadane.summary: Tracks a best local prefix and a global optimum in a single linear pass.

linear-search.title: Linear Search
linear-search.summary: Traverses the array sequentially and serves as a minimal reference for iterative searches.

maximum-subarray-cuadratico.title: Quadratic Maximum Subarray
maximum-subarray-cuadratico.summary: Iterates over all starting points and expands running sums to contrast with Kadane.

merge-dos-arreglos-ordenados.title: Merge two sorted arrays
merge-dos-arreglos-ordenados.summary: Uses two pointers and a temporary output to study a classic linear merge.

newton-raphson-iterativo.title: Iterative Newton-Raphson
newton-raphson-iterativo.summary: Numerical sample with successive refinements and a tolerance-based stopping rule.

pascal-triangle-bottom-up.title: Bottom-up Pascal Triangle
pascal-triangle-bottom-up.summary: Tabular construction of a triangular matrix; it stays in the master catalog for now but not in the public UI.

prefix-sum.title: Prefix Sum
prefix-sum.summary: Builds a reusable cumulative sum and is ideal to study simple linear dependencies.

selection-sort.title: Selection Sort
selection-sort.summary: Finds the remaining minimum and places it at the front on each iteration.

shell-sort.title: Shell Sort
shell-sort.summary: Refines the array through decreasing gaps and shows multiple levels of iterative nesting.

sieve-of-eratosthenes.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
sieve-of-eratosthenes.summary: Marks multiples in a boolean table and works well to study nested loops with jumps.

suma-de-arreglo.title: Array sum
suma-de-arreglo.summary: Accumulates every element in the array in a single linear scan.

ternary-search-iterativo.title: Iterative Ternary Search
ternary-search-iterativo.summary: Splits the range into three sections per iteration over a sorted array.

two-sum-con-hash.title: Two Sum with hash
two-sum-con-hash.summary: Lives in the master catalog as a reminder for richer auxiliary-object support in the future.

warshall-transitive-closure.title: Warshall Transitive Closure
warshall-transitive-closure.summary: Triple loop over a matrix; remains disabled until two-dimensional matrix support is validated more carefully.

closest-pair-of-points.title: Closest Pair of Points
closest-pair-of-points.summary: A geometrically faithful skeleton that stays hidden until the strip and point handling is modeled more tightly.

convex-hull-divide-and-conquer.title: Divide-and-Conquer Convex Hull
convex-hull-divide-and-conquer.summary: Kept as a reference sketch for a future validated divide-and-conquer convex hull sample.

cooley-tukey-fft.title: Cooley-Tukey FFT
cooley-tukey-fft.summary: Recursive FFT over even and odd terms; stays disabled until a more parser-friendly version is fixed.

counting-inversions.title: Counting Inversions
counting-inversions.summary: Splits the array, counts on each half, and accumulates cross inversions while merging.

fast-multipole-skeleton-simplificado.title: Simplified Fast Multipole Skeleton
fast-multipole-skeleton-simplificado.summary: Kept as an honest placeholder for a hierarchical pattern that is not ready for end-user exposure yet.

karatsuba-multiplication.title: Karatsuba Multiplication
karatsuba-multiplication.summary: Shows a ternary split of the multiplication work with an algebraic combine phase at the end.

kth-smallest-mediana-de-medianas.title: K-th Smallest by Median of Medians
kth-smallest-mediana-de-medianas.summary: Kept as an advanced reference until a tighter deterministic-pivot variant is ready to publish.

majority-element-divide-and-conquer.title: Divide-and-Conquer Majority Element
majority-element-divide-and-conquer.summary: Obtains candidates per half and validates them in the combine phase.

matrix-chain-parenthesization-divide-and.title: Naive Divide-and-Conquer Matrix Chain Parenthesization
matrix-chain-parenthesization-divide-and.summary: Naive recursive matrix partition model kept out of the UI while we validate a more stable form.

max-min-tournament.title: Max-Min Tournament
max-min-tournament.summary: Splits the array into two halves and combines the maximum and minimum from each branch.

merge-sort.title: Merge Sort
merge-sort.summary: Splits the array in half, sorts each half, and merges them in linear time.

minimax-de-arbol-binario.title: Binary Tree Minimax
minimax-de-arbol-binario.summary: Recursive game-tree sketch kept out of the UI until auxiliary node handling is tightened.

nearest-points-by-strip-merge-variant.title: Nearest Points by Strip Merge Variant
nearest-points-by-strip-merge-variant.summary: A strip-based nearest-points variant kept as an advanced draft in the master catalog.

polynomial-multiplication-divide-and-con.title: Divide-and-Conquer Polynomial Multiplication
polynomial-multiplication-divide-and-con.summary: Splits the polynomials in halves and combines partial products at the end.

post-office-recursive-partition.title: Post Office Recursive Partition
post-office-recursive-partition.summary: Recursive interval-partition placeholder that is not public yet because it needs a more concrete form.

quadtree-construction.title: QuadTree Construction
quadtree-construction.summary: Four-way matrix partition kept for now as a master-catalog reference only.

quick-sort.title: Quick Sort
quick-sort.summary: Partitions around a pivot and solves the two remaining regions recursively.

range-sum-query-divide-and-conquer.title: Divide-and-Conquer Range Sum Query
range-sum-query-divide-and-conquer.summary: Shows range partition into two halves, but stays out of the UI until a tighter version is ready.

segment-tree-construction.title: Segment Tree Construction
segment-tree-construction.summary: Recursive interval construction reserved for a fuller future version.

skyline-problem-divide-and-conquer.title: Divide-and-Conquer Skyline Problem
skyline-problem-divide-and-conquer.summary: Classic skyline merge problem that remains an advanced record for now.

strassen-matrix-multiplication.title: Strassen Matrix Multiplication
strassen-matrix-multiplication.summary: Included in the master catalog but still disabled until the matrix representation is refined.

tournament-tree-construction.title: Tournament Tree Construction
tournament-tree-construction.summary: Splits the array into two branches and combines local winners at the root.

vlsi-closest-pair-style-partition.title: VLSI Closest-Pair Style Partition
vlsi-closest-pair-style-partition.summary: Advanced geometric partition variant stored only in the master catalog for now.

weighted-median-divide-and-conquer.title: Divide-and-Conquer Weighted Median
weighted-median-divide-and-conquer.summary: Kept as an advanced weighted selection sample, still out of the public UI.

z-order-recursive-matrix-traversal.title: Recursive Z-order Matrix Traversal
z-order-recursive-matrix-traversal.summary: Traverses a matrix by quadrants and makes a clear four-way divide-and-conquer pattern visible.

binary-search-recursiva.title: Recursive Binary Search
binary-search-recursiva.summary: Reduces the range to a single half and is one of the most reliable cases in the recursive catalog.

binary-tree-height.title: Binary Tree Height
binary-tree-height.summary: Kept in the master catalog, but its two-branch shape stays out of the initial release.

euclides-recursivo.title: Recursive Euclid
euclides-recursivo.summary: A short, stable case for reduction by modulo until the final divisor is reached.

exponenciacion-rapida.title: Fast Exponentiation
exponenciacion-rapida.summary: Reduces the exponent by half on each call and reuses the central subresult.

fibonacci-search-recursiva.title: Recursive Fibonacci Search
